- [CheckIfPhoneNumberIsOptedOut](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sns/checkifphonenumberisoptedout) — Runtime binding for `sns:CheckIfPhoneNumberIsOptedOut`.
- [CheckInLicense](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/licensemanager/checkinlicense) — Runtime binding for `license-manager:CheckInLicense` — return a previously checked-out entitlement to the license pool using the consumption token from CheckoutLicense.
- [CheckNoNewAccess](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/accessanalyzer/checknonewaccess) — Runtime binding for `access-analyzer:CheckNoNewAccess`.
- [CheckNoPublicAccess](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/accessanalyzer/checknopublicaccess) — Runtime binding for `access-analyzer:CheckNoPublicAccess`.
- [CheckoutBorrowLicense](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/licensemanager/checkoutborrowlicense) — Runtime binding for `license-manager:CheckoutBorrowLicense` — check out an offline-capable (borrow) entitlement from a seller-issued license that allows borrowing. The signed token proves the entitlement while the consumer is disconnected.
- [CheckoutLicense](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/licensemanager/checkoutlicense) — Runtime binding for `license-manager:CheckoutLicense` — check out entitlements from a seller-issued license for the calling application. The returned `LicenseConsumptionToken` is used to check in or extend the consumption; `PROVISIONAL` checkouts expire and must be extended with ExtendLicenseConsumption.
- [CisScanConfiguration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/inspector2/cisscanconfiguration) — An Amazon Inspector CIS scan configuration — schedules CIS Benchmark scans of SSM-managed EC2 instances selected by resource tags. Name, level, schedule, and targets are all updatable in place; identity is the configuration's ARN.
- [ClassificationJob](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/macie2/classificationjob) — An Amazon Macie classification job — scans one or more S3 buckets for sensitive data. Requires Macie to be enabled for the account (see `Macie2.Session`). Jobs are immutable once created; changing the job type, name, or bucket set replaces the job. Destroy cancels the job.
- [ClassifyDocument](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/comprehend/classifydocument) — Runtime binding for `comprehend:ClassifyDocument` — classify a single document in real time against a custom classifier endpoint or a Comprehend prebuilt model ARN (`EndpointArn`).
- [ClearQuerySuggestions](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kendra/clearquerysuggestions) — Runtime binding for the `ClearQuerySuggestions` operation (IAM action `kendra:ClearQuerySuggestions`), scoped to one Index.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudhsmv2/cluster) — An AWS CloudHSM cluster — a fleet of FIPS-validated, single-tenant hardware security modules (HSMs) inside your VPC.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/dax/cluster) — An Amazon DAX cluster — a fully managed, in-memory write-through cache for DynamoDB.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/dsql/cluster) — An Amazon Aurora DSQL cluster — a serverless, distributed SQL database with active-active high availability and Postgres wire compatibility.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/docdbelastic/cluster) — An Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster — a MongoDB-compatible, sharded document database that scales workloads to millions of reads/writes per second without managing instances.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ecs/cluster) — An Amazon ECS cluster for running tasks and services.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eks/cluster) — An Amazon EKS cluster with support for EKS Auto Mode settings.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/emr/cluster) — A provisioned Amazon EMR cluster (job flow) running open-source big-data frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop on EC2 instances.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/memorydb/cluster) — An Amazon MemoryDB cluster — a durable, Redis/Valkey-compatible in-memory database.
- [Cluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/redshift/cluster) — A provisioned Amazon Redshift data-warehouse cluster.
- [ClusterParameterGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/redshift/clusterparametergroup) — An Amazon Redshift cluster parameter group — a named set of database parameters applied to provisioned Redshift clusters.
- [ClusterPolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/dsql/clusterpolicy) — The resource-based policy of an Aurora DSQL cluster — controls which principals may perform actions on the cluster (most commonly gating `dsql:DbConnect` / `dsql:DbConnectAdmin` behind VPC or Organization conditions). A cluster has at most one.
- [ClusterSubnetGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/redshift/clustersubnetgroup) — An Amazon Redshift cluster subnet group — the set of VPC subnets a provisioned Redshift cluster's nodes are placed into.
- [CodeHookEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lexv2/codehookeventsource) — Event source connecting an Amazon Lex V2 bot alias's Lambda code hook (dialog and fulfillment) to the hosting Lambda function.
- [CodeInterpreter](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockagentcore/codeinterpreter) — A custom Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter — an isolated sandbox where agents execute Python/JavaScript/TypeScript code.
- [Collection](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/opensearchserverless/collection) — An Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection — a group of OpenSearch indexes that scales OpenSearch Compute Units (OCUs) automatically. A collection of type `VECTORSEARCH` is the vector store required to back an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base.
- [CollectionGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/opensearchserverless/collectiongroup) — An Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection group. Collection groups manage OpenSearch Compute Units (OCUs) at a group level — multiple collections share the group's capacity limits instead of each collection scaling independently.
- [CommitTransaction](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/rdsdata/committransaction) — Runtime binding for `rds-data:CommitTransaction` — commit a Data API transaction opened with `AWS.RDSData.BeginTransaction`.

- [CompositeAlarm](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudwatch/compositealarm) — A CloudWatch composite alarm — combines the states of other alarms with a boolean `AlarmRule` expression so a single alarm (and its actions) reflects overall health.
- [ComputeEnvironment](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/batch/computeenvironment) — An AWS Batch managed compute environment backed by Fargate (or Fargate Spot) capacity. Fargate compute environments provision in seconds and require no instance management.
- [ConditionalForwarder](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/directoryservice/conditionalforwarder) — A conditional forwarder on an AWS Managed Microsoft AD (or AD Connector) directory — forwards DNS queries for a remote domain to that domain's DNS servers. Conditional forwarders are the prerequisite for trust relationships with other domains.
- [ConfigRule](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/config/configrule) — An AWS Config rule that evaluates whether your AWS resources comply with a desired configuration — either an AWS-managed rule, a custom Lambda rule, or a Guard custom-policy rule.
- [Configuration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mq/configuration) — An Amazon MQ broker configuration — a versioned document (ActiveMQ XML or RabbitMQ Cuttlefish) that a Broker can reference to control engine-level settings. Each edit to `data` publishes a new immutable revision; a broker pins a specific `{ id, revision }` pair.

- [Connection](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/codeconnections/connection) — An AWS CodeConnections connection to a source-code provider (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket).
- [Connection](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eventbridge/connection) — An Amazon EventBridge connection holding the authorization used to invoke an HTTP endpoint through an ApiDestination. EventBridge stores the secret half of the connection in Secrets Manager on your behalf.
- [Connection](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/glue/connection) — An AWS Glue connection — stores the connection details (JDBC URL, VPC networking, credentials) that crawlers and jobs use to reach a data store.
- [ConnectorProfile](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/appflow/connectorprofile) — An Amazon AppFlow connector profile. A connector profile stores the connection settings and credentials for a SaaS/data-warehouse connector (Salesforce, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.) so flows can reference it.
- [ConnectRead](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/dax/connectread) — Read-only runtime access to a DAX Cluster's data plane.
- [ConnectRead](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kafka/connectread) — Read-only (consumer) runtime access to an MSK ServerlessCluster's data plane.
- [Contact](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ssmcontacts/contact) — An Incident Manager contact — a person Incident Manager engages during an incident, an escalation plan that engages contacts in phases, or an on-call schedule backed by rotations.
- [ContactChannel](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ssmcontacts/contactchannel) — An Incident Manager contact channel — the method (SMS, voice, or email) that Incident Manager uses to engage a contact during an incident.
- [ContactInformation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/account/contactinformation) — The primary contact information of an AWS account — the account-global mailing address and phone number AWS uses to reach the account owner. Every account has exactly one primary contact; this resource upserts it via `account:PutContactInformation`. AWS does not allow deleting the primary contact, so destroying the resource stops managing it and leaves the last value in place.
- [ContainsPiiEntities](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/comprehend/containspiientities) — Runtime binding for `comprehend:ContainsPiiEntities` — check whether the input text contains personally identifiable information, returning the PII entity-type labels present (without offsets; use DetectPiiEntities to locate them).

Provide the implementation with `Effect.provide(AWS.Personalize.CreateSolutionHttp)`.

Provide the implementation with `Effect.provide(AWS.Personalize.CreateSolutionVersionHttp)`.

The token (a claims-based JWT, `Redacted` end-to-end) is distributed to license consumers, who exchange it for temporary credentials with `GetAccessToken` + `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`.

- [Crl](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/rolesanywhere/crl) — An IAM Roles Anywhere certificate revocation list (CRL). A CRL is a PEM-encoded list of certificates revoked by the trust anchor's certificate authority; IAM Roles Anywhere refuses to vend credentials for revoked certificates while the CRL is enabled.
- [CustomAction](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/chatbot/customaction) — An AWS Chatbot (Amazon Q Developer in chat applications) custom action — a reusable CLI command that chat users invoke by alias or as a button on notifications.
- [CustomDataIdentifier](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/macie2/customdataidentifier) — An Amazon Macie custom data identifier — a regex-based detection criterion (with optional keywords, ignore words, and severity thresholds) that classification jobs and automated discovery use to detect organization- specific sensitive data. Requires Macie to be enabled for the account (see `Macie2.Session`). Definitions are immutable: any change other than tags replaces the identifier. Destroy soft-deletes it.
- [CustomLogSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/securitylake/customlogsource) — A custom (third-party) log source registered with Amazon Security Lake. Security Lake provisions a Glue crawler, database, and table for the source, plus an IAM role the provider assumes to write OCSF-formatted data into the data lake. Requires `SecurityLake.DataLake` to already be enabled in the Region.
- [Dashboard](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudwatch/dashboard) — An Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. The `DashboardBody` is a structured, typed document (metric, text, alarm-status, and log widgets) that the provider serializes to the JSON string CloudWatch expects.
- [Dashboard](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/quicksight/dashboard) — An Amazon QuickSight dashboard — a published, read-only view built from a template, an analysis, or an inline definition.

- [DataAutomationProject](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockdataautomation/dataautomationproject) — An Amazon Bedrock Data Automation Project — the configuration unit that turns documents, images, audio, and video into structured output, with optional custom output driven by `Blueprint`s.
- [Database](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/glue/database) — An AWS Glue Data Catalog database — the top-level container for Glue tables that Athena, EMR, Redshift Spectrum, and Glue jobs query. Databases are free and instant to create.
- [Database](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/timestream/database) — An Amazon Timestream for LiveAnalytics database — the top-level container for time-series Tables.
- [DataCatalog](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/athena/datacatalog) — An Amazon Athena data catalog — registers an external metadata source (a federated Lambda connector, an external Hive metastore, or a cross-account Glue Data Catalog) that Athena queries can reference as a `catalog`.
- [DataCellsFilter](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lakeformation/datacellsfilter) — A Lake Formation data cells filter — row- and column-level security on a Glue table. Grant `SELECT` on the filter (via `Resource.DataCellsFilter`) to give principals access to only the filtered cells.
- [DataIntegration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/appintegrations/dataintegration) — An Amazon AppIntegrations data integration. Data integrations reference an external data source (an S3 bucket, or a SaaS application through Amazon AppFlow) so services like Amazon Q in Connect can ingest its content.
- [DataLake](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/securitylake/datalake) — The Amazon Security Lake data lake — the account-wide singleton that onboards the account to Security Lake. Enabling it creates S3 buckets, registers them with Lake Formation, and configures the Glue metastore in every configured Region.
- [DataLakeSettings](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lakeformation/datalakesettings) — The Lake Formation data lake settings for the account — an account/region singleton controlling who the data lake administrators are, the default permissions for new databases/tables, and external data filtering.
- [Dataset](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/databrew/dataset) — An AWS Glue DataBrew dataset — a pointer to source data (S3 file/prefix, Glue Data Catalog table, or JDBC query) plus parsing options. The dataset definition itself stores no data and is free; it is consumed by DataBrew projects and jobs.
- [Dataset](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/forecast/dataset) — An Amazon Forecast dataset — a typed, domain-scoped collection of time-series (or metadata) records described by a schema. Creating the dataset is a cheap metadata operation; bulk imports and training happen through separate import jobs and predictors.
- [Dataset](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/personalize/dataset) — An Amazon Personalize dataset — a typed collection (Interactions, Items, Users, …) inside a dataset group, backed by a schema. Creating the dataset is a cheap metadata operation; bulk imports and training happen through separate import jobs and solutions.
- [DataSet](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/dataexchange/dataset) — An AWS Data Exchange data set — the top-level container that data providers publish revisions of data into. An owned data set holds revisions, each of which holds assets (e.g. S3 snapshot files) that subscribers receive.
- [DataSet](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/quicksight/dataset) — An Amazon QuickSight dataset — a prepared, queryable model built on top of one or more data sources.
- [DatasetGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/forecast/datasetgroup) — An Amazon Forecast dataset group — a domain-scoped container that groups the datasets used to train predictors. Creating the group is cheap; the expensive training work lives in predictors and forecasts provisioned separately.
- [DatasetGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/personalize/datasetgroup) — An Amazon Personalize dataset group — the top-level container that holds the datasets, solutions, and campaigns for a single use case. Creating a dataset group is cheap and fast; the expensive training work lives in solutions and campaigns provisioned separately.

- [Deployment](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/appconfig/deployment) — An AWS AppConfig deployment — releases a configuration version to an environment following a deployment strategy. Deployments are immutable and asynchronous: the provider starts the deployment and waits (bounded) for it to reach a terminal state. Any change to the deployed version, strategy, or target creates a new deployment (a replacement). Use an all-at-once strategy (duration 0, bake 0) for a near-instant rollout.

Deployment configurations are immutable: any change replaces the configuration.
- [DeploymentEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/appconfig/deploymenteventsource) — Event source connecting AppConfig deployment notifications to the hosting compute. The contract is a `Binding.Service`; the Lambda implementation layer is `Lambda.AppConfigDeploymentEventSource` (extension + association + invoke role at deploy time, payload dispatch at runtime). Consume it through the consumeDeploymentEvents helper.
- [DeploymentGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/codedeploy/deploymentgroup) — An AWS CodeDeploy deployment group — the set of target instances/functions plus the deployment configuration for one Application. - [Detector](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/guardduty/detector) — A GuardDuty detector — the account/region singleton that enables Amazon GuardDuty threat detection. Only one detector can exist per region, so this resource is a capture-and-restore singleton: adopting a pre-existing detector that Alchemy did not create requires `--adopt`.
- [DetectorVersion](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/frauddetector/detectorversion) — An Amazon Fraud Detector detector version — the deployable revision of a detector. It bundles a set of rules (owned inline here) over the detector's event type and, when `ACTIVE`, serves real-time predictions via `getEventPrediction`. Rules and the version are cheap, rule-based configuration objects — no model training is involved.

Attach a custom set to a VPC to override the AWS defaults — for example to point instances at your own DNS or an internal search domain.

- [DisconnectUser](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ivschat/disconnectuser) — Moderate the bound room by disconnecting all WebSocket connections of a user — the effectful call made from a deployed Lambda or Task. The `userId` is the one the user's chat token was minted with; disconnection does not prevent reconnection, so revoke by not minting further tokens. The call succeeds even when the user has no open connections.

Poll it as a cheap change detector and re-call `DiscoverInstances` only when the revision moves. Provide the implementation with `Effect.provide(AWS.CloudMap.DiscoverInstancesRevisionHttp)`.

- [DurableFunction](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lambda/durablefunction) — An AWS Lambda Durable Function — a code-first, replay-based orchestrator that IS a durable Lambda Function. `AWS.Lambda.DurableFunction` is a wrapper of Function: it owns the underlying Lambda function, configures its `DurableConfig` at `CreateFunction` (durability is a create-time property — a DurableFunction is always durable), registers the durable-execution listener on the owned entrypoint, self-binds the checkpoint-protocol IAM (`lambda:CheckpointDurableExecution`, `lambda:GetDurableExecutionState`) onto the execution role, and vendors the open-source `@aws/durable-execution-sdk-js` into the artifact (install it in your project: `npm i @aws/durable-execution-sdk-js`).
- [EgressOnlyInternetGateway](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/egressonlyinternetgateway) — An egress-only internet gateway is the IPv6 counterpart to a NAT gateway: it lets instances in a VPC initiate outbound IPv6 traffic to the internet while preventing the internet from initiating inbound connections to them. Use it to give private, IPv6-addressed resources outbound-only internet access.

- [FileSystem](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/fsx/filesystem) — An Amazon FSx file system — fully-managed shared storage for Lustre, Windows File Server, NetApp ONTAP, or OpenZFS.
- [FileSystem](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/s3files/filesystem) — An Amazon S3 File System — POSIX-style file system access over an S3 general purpose bucket (mountable from EC2/ECS via mount targets, with application-scoped access via AccessPoints).
- [Filter](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/guardduty/filter) — A GuardDuty findings filter — matches findings against criteria and either keeps (`NOOP`) or auto-archives (`ARCHIVE`) them. Identity is the `(detectorId, name)` pair; description, action, rank, and criteria are updatable in place.
- [Filter](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/inspector2/filter) — An Amazon Inspector findings filter — matches findings against criteria and either keeps them visible (`NONE`, a saved view) or suppresses them (`SUPPRESS`, a suppression rule). Everything is updatable in place; the filter's identity is its ARN.
- [FilterLogEvents](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/logs/filterlogevents) — Runtime binding for `logs:FilterLogEvents`.
- [FindingAggregator](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/securityhub/findingaggregator) — The Security Hub cross-Region finding aggregator — replicates findings from linked Regions into the home Region. Only one aggregator can exist per account, so this is a singleton: adopting a pre-existing aggregator that Alchemy did not create requires `--adopt`.
- [FindingsFilter](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/macie2/findingsfilter) — An Amazon Macie findings filter — matches findings against criteria and either keeps (`NOOP`) or auto-suppresses (`ARCHIVE`) them. Requires Macie to be enabled for the account (see `Macie2.Session`). Name, description, action, position, and criteria are all updatable in place.
- [Firewall](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/networkfirewall/firewall) — An AWS Network Firewall firewall — provisions managed firewall endpoints into your VPC subnets and inspects traffic according to an associated FirewallPolicy.
- [FirewallPolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/networkfirewall/firewallpolicy) — An AWS Network Firewall policy — defines a firewall's traffic inspection behavior as a collection of stateless and stateful rule group references plus default actions. One policy can be shared by multiple firewalls.
- [Fleet](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/deadline/fleet) — An AWS Deadline Cloud fleet — a group of workers (customer-managed hosts or service-managed EC2 instances) that run render jobs from associated queues.
- [Fleet](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iotfleetwise/fleet) — An AWS IoT FleetWise fleet — a group of vehicles that campaigns can target collectively.
- [Flow](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/appflow/flow) — An Amazon AppFlow flow. A flow transfers data between a source connector and one or more destination connectors, applying field-mapping tasks. The credential-free S3-to-S3 path is directly testable; other connectors require a ConnectorProfile with vendor credentials.
- [Flow](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mediaconnect/flow) — An AWS Elemental MediaConnect flow — a reliable live-video transport between a source and one or more outputs.
- [FlowLog](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/flowlog) — A flow log captures information about the IP traffic going to and from a VPC, subnet, or network interface, and publishes it to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use it for network monitoring, traffic analysis, and troubleshooting security-group / NACL rules.

- [InvokeAgent](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrock/invokeagent) — Runtime binding for `bedrock-agent-runtime:InvokeAgent` — send user input to a Bedrock agent through one of its aliases and receive the agent's response as an event stream.
- [InvokeAgentRuntime](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockagentcore/invokeagentruntime) — Sends a request to an agent hosted in an AgentCore Runtime and receives the (optionally streaming) response.
- [InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockagentcore/invokeagentruntimecommand) — Runs a shell command inside an agent hosted in an AgentCore Runtime and streams back the command output.
- [InvokeBlueprintOptimizationAsync](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockdataautomation/invokeblueprintoptimizationasync) — Runtime binding for the `InvokeBlueprintOptimizationAsync` operation (IAM action `bedrock:InvokeBlueprintOptimizationAsync` on the blueprint ARN + the account's data automation profiles) — start an asynchronous job that tunes the bound blueprint's schema against labeled samples (asset + ground-truth pairs in S3) from a deployed Function.
- [InvokeBrowser](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockagentcore/invokebrowser) — Performs an OS-level browser action (mouse, keyboard, screenshot) in a session.
- [InvokeCodeInterpreter](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockagentcore/invokecodeinterpreter) — Executes a tool (e.g. `executeCode`) inside a code interpreter session. The response carries a result stream.
- [InvokeDataAutomation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockdataautomation/invokedataautomation) — Runtime binding for the synchronous `InvokeDataAutomation` operation (IAM action `bedrock:InvokeDataAutomation` on the project ARN + the account's data automation profiles) — process a file inline against the bound project from a deployed Function and get the extracted output back in the response.
- [InvokeDataAutomationAsync](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockdataautomation/invokedataautomationasync) — Runtime binding for the `InvokeDataAutomationAsync` operation (IAM action `bedrock:InvokeDataAutomationAsync` on the project ARN + the account's data automation profiles) — start an asynchronous Bedrock Data Automation job against the bound project from a deployed Function.
- [InvokeDataAutomationLibraryIngestionJob](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrockdataautomation/invokedataautomationlibraryingestionjob) — Runtime binding for the `InvokeDataAutomationLibraryIngestionJob` operation (IAM action `bedrock:InvokeDataAutomationLibraryIngestionJob` on the library ARN) — start an asynchronous ingestion job that upserts or deletes entities in the bound library from a deployed Function.
- [InvokeEndpoint](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sagemakerruntime/invokeendpoint) — Runtime binding for `sagemaker:InvokeEndpoint` — run real-time inference against a deployed SageMaker endpoint with a model-native request body.
- [InvokeEndpointAsync](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sagemakerruntime/invokeendpointasync) — Runtime binding for `sagemaker:InvokeEndpointAsync` — enqueue an asynchronous inference request against a deployed SageMaker async endpoint. The request payload is read from S3 (`InputLocation`) and the result is written back to S3; the call returns immediately with an `OutputLocation`.
- [InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sagemakerruntime/invokeendpointwithresponsestream) — Runtime binding for `sagemaker:InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream` — the streaming variant of InvokeEndpoint. The inference response arrives incrementally as an event `Stream` of `PayloadPart` events carrying raw model-specific bytes; the container behind the endpoint must support inference streaming.
- [InvokeModel](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrock/invokemodel) — Runtime binding for `bedrock-runtime:InvokeModel` — run inference with a model-specific request body (text, image, or embedding models).
- [InvokeModelWithResponseStream](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrock/invokemodelwithresponsestream) — Runtime binding for `bedrock-runtime:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` — the streaming variant of InvokeModel. The response arrives as an event `Stream` of `chunk` events carrying model-specific payload bytes.
- [InvokeRestApi](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mwaa/invokerestapi) — Runtime binding for `airflow:InvokeRestApi` (Airflow 2.4.3+).
- [InvokeWithResponseStream](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lambda/invokewithresponsestream) — Runtime binding for `lambda:InvokeFunction` over the response-streaming API. Invokes the bound Function and returns the streaming response — `EventStream` yields `PayloadChunk` events followed by a final `InvokeComplete` event.
- [IPSet](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/guardduty/ipset) — A GuardDuty trusted IP set — an S3-hosted list of IP addresses GuardDuty treats as trusted, suppressing findings for traffic from them. The list file must exist in S3 before activation; name, location, and activation are updatable in place, while format changes replace the set.
- [IPSet](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/wafv2/ipset) — An AWS WAFv2 IP set — a named collection of IP addresses and CIDR ranges referenced from web ACL and rule group rules via `IPSetReferenceStatement`.
- [IsAuthorized](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/verifiedpermissions/isauthorized) — Runtime binding for Verified Permissions authorization — bind it to a `PolicyStore` inside a function runtime to get a client that evaluates authorization requests against the store's Cedar policies.
- [IsMemberInGroups](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/identitycenter/ismemberingroups) — Runtime binding for the `IsMemberInGroups` operation (IAM action `identitystore:IsMemberInGroups`), scoped to one Instance.
- [IssueCertificate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/acmpca/issuecertificate) — Runtime binding for `acm-pca:IssueCertificate`.
- [Job](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/databrew/job) — An AWS Glue DataBrew job definition — either a `PROFILE` job that analyzes a dataset and writes a data-quality profile to S3, or a `RECIPE` job that applies a published recipe's transformations and writes the result to S3. The definition is free and instant; job *runs* are billed per node-hour and are started with `StartJobRun`.
- [Job](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/glue/job) — An AWS Glue job — a Spark (`glueetl`), Python shell (`pythonshell`), or streaming ETL job definition (script in S3 + IAM role + arguments). The definition lifecycle is instant and free; job *runs* are billed and are started via `startJobRun`.
- [Job](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mediaconvert/job) — An AWS Elemental MediaConvert transcode job — a one-shot request to convert an input in S3 into one or more outputs. Jobs are immutable once submitted: they run to `COMPLETE`, `ERROR`, or `CANCELED` on their own. Deleting the resource cancels the job only if it is still `SUBMITTED` or `PROGRESSING`.
- [JobDefinition](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/batch/jobdefinition) — An AWS Batch job definition for Fargate container jobs. Job definitions are immutable revisions — changing the container configuration registers a new revision under the same name (like ECS task definitions); destroying the resource deregisters every active revision.
- [JobQueue](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/batch/jobqueue) — An AWS Batch job queue. Jobs submitted to the queue are scheduled onto its associated compute environments in preference order.
- [JobTemplate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/emrcontainers/jobtemplate) — An Amazon EMR on EKS job template — a stored set of `StartJobRun` values (execution role, release label, job driver, configuration) that can be referenced by ID when starting job runs, optionally with `${placeholder}` parameters filled in per run.
- [JobTemplate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mediaconvert/jobtemplate) — An AWS Elemental MediaConvert job template — a reusable, named transcode configuration (inputs, output groups, and job-level settings) that new jobs are created from so callers only supply the input/output specifics.
- [JoinStorageSession](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kinesisvideo/joinstoragesession) — Runtime binding for `kinesisvideo:JoinStorageSession` (WebRTC storage data plane).
- [JoinStorageSessionAsViewer](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kinesisvideo/joinstoragesessionasviewer) — Runtime binding for `kinesisvideo:JoinStorageSessionAsViewer` (WebRTC storage data plane).
- [KafkaEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kafka/kafkaeventsource) — Event source connecting topics on an MSK `ServerlessCluster` to the hosting compute.
- [Key](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/key) — An AWS Payment Cryptography key — a managed cryptographic key with TR-31 attributes (algorithm, class, usage, modes of use) used for data encryption, MAC generation/verification, and other payment-domain cryptographic operations.
- [KeyGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudfront/keygroup) — A CloudFront key group.
- [KeyPair](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/keypair) — An EC2 key pair used to grant SSH access to instances launched with its `keyName`.
- [Keyspace](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/keyspaces/keyspace) — An Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) keyspace — the top-level container for Cassandra tables.
- [KeyValueStore](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudfront/keyvaluestore) — A CloudFront KeyValueStore for edge metadata.
- [KnowledgeBase](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/bedrock/knowledgebase) — An Amazon Bedrock knowledge base — a managed RAG index that embeds source documents into a vector store for retrieval.
- [KvEntries](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudfront/kventries) — Manages namespaced key-value entries in a CloudFront KeyValueStore.
- [KvRoutesUpdate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudfront/kvroutesupdate) — Manages a single route entry in a JSON array stored in a CloudFront KeyValueStore.
- [KxCluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/finspace/kxcluster) — A kdb cluster inside an Amazon FinSpace Managed kdb environment — the compute that mounts kdb databases and serves q queries.
- [KxDatabase](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/finspace/kxdatabase) — A kdb database inside an Amazon FinSpace Managed kdb environment — the versioned, changeset-based store that kdb clusters mount and query.
- [KxEnvironment](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/finspace/kxenvironment) — An Amazon FinSpace Managed kdb environment — the account-level container that kdb databases, clusters, users, volumes and scaling groups live in.
- [Label](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/frauddetector/label) — An Amazon Fraud Detector label — a classification (e.g. `fraud`, `legit`) used to tag stored events for supervised model training. Event types reference labels; they are cheap metadata objects.

- [LambdaCodeHookEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lexv2/lambdacodehookeventsource) — Connects an Amazon Lex V2 bot alias's Lambda code hook to the current Lambda function.
- [LandingZone](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/controltower/landingzone) — An AWS Control Tower landing zone — the org-wide multi-account environment (organization structure, governed regions, centralized logging, and access management) that Control Tower governs.
- [LaunchTemplate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/autoscaling/launchtemplate) — A launch template that preserves the `Host` authoring model used by `AWS.EC2.Instance`, but packages that host configuration for use with an Auto Scaling Group.
- [Lexicon](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/polly/lexicon) — An Amazon Polly pronunciation lexicon — a W3C PLS document stored in a region that customizes how `SynthesizeSpeech` pronounces specific words. Identity is the region-scoped `lexiconName`; the PLS `content` is updatable in place.
- [LFTag](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lakeformation/lftag) — A Lake Formation LF-tag definition — a key with a list of allowed values used for tag-based access control (attach values to databases/tables with AWS.LakeFormation.LFTagAssociation, grant on expressions with AWS.LakeFormation.Permissions).
- [LFTagAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lakeformation/lftagassociation) — Attaches LF-tag values to a Data Catalog resource (database, table, or columns) for Lake Formation tag-based access control.
- [LFTagExpression](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lakeformation/lftagexpression) — A named Lake Formation LF-tag expression — a reusable, saved combination of LF-tag conditions that can be referenced from permission grants (`Resource.LFTagExpression`) instead of repeating the raw expression.
- [LicenseConfiguration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/licensemanager/licenseconfiguration) — An AWS License Manager license configuration — an abstraction of a customer license agreement that License Manager can track and enforce.
- [LifecycleHook](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/autoscaling/lifecyclehook) — A lifecycle hook that pauses an Auto Scaling instance in a wait state on launch or termination so a handler can drain connections, snapshot state, or warm caches before the transition completes. Pair with consumeLifecycleActions to receive the transition events and CompleteLifecycleAction to signal `CONTINUE` / `ABANDON`.
- [LifecyclePolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/dlm/lifecyclepolicy) — An Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) lifecycle policy that automates the creation, retention, and deletion of EBS snapshots or EBS-backed AMIs.
- [LifecyclePolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/opensearchserverless/lifecyclepolicy) — An Amazon OpenSearch Serverless data lifecycle policy. Retention lifecycle policies control how long documents are retained in the indexes matched by the policy's resource patterns — OpenSearch Serverless automatically deletes documents older than the configured `MinIndexRetention`.
- [Link](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/oam/link) — A CloudWatch cross-account observability **link** — created in a source account, it attaches to a monitoring-account Sink and shares the selected telemetry types (metrics, log groups, traces, Application Signals) with that account.

- [PlaceIndex](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/location/placeindex) — An Amazon Location Service place index. A place index geocodes text and positions against a chosen data provider. The data source is immutable; the intended use and description can be updated in place.
- [Plan](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ssmcontacts/plan) — The engagement plan of an Incident Manager contact — the staged sequence of contact channels (for `PERSONAL` contacts), contacts (for `ESCALATION` plans), or rotations (for `ONCALL_SCHEDULE` contacts) that Incident Manager engages during an incident.
- [PlatformApplication](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sns/platformapplication) — An Amazon SNS platform application for mobile push notifications (FCM, APNS, ADM, Baidu).
- [PlaybackConfiguration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mediatailor/playbackconfiguration) — An AWS Elemental MediaTailor playback configuration for server-side ad insertion (SSAI) into HLS and DASH video streams.
- [PlaybackKeyPair](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ivs/playbackkeypair) — An Amazon IVS playback key pair for private channels.
- [PlaybackRestrictionPolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ivs/playbackrestrictionpolicy) — An Amazon IVS playback restriction policy, constraining channel playback by viewer country and/or request origin.
- [PodIdentityAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eks/podidentityassociation) — An Amazon EKS pod identity association that binds a service account to an IAM role.
- [PodIdentityServiceAccount](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eks/podidentityserviceaccount) — Creates a Kubernetes service account and binds it to EKS Pod Identity.
- [PodIdentityWorkload](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eks/podidentityworkload) — Creates a pod-identity-enabled workload on an EKS cluster.
- [Policy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iam/policy) — A customer-managed IAM policy.
- [Policy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iot/policy) — An AWS IoT policy that grants MQTT permissions (connect, publish, subscribe, receive) to certificates and other principals.
- [Policy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/organizations/policy) — An AWS Organizations policy such as an SCP or tag policy.
- [Policy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/verifiedpermissions/policy) — A static Cedar policy in a Verified Permissions policy store. Static policies contain a complete Cedar statement and are evaluated for every matching authorization request.
- [PolicyAttachment](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/organizations/policyattachment) — Attaches an Organizations Policy to a root, OU, or account.
- [PolicyStore](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/verifiedpermissions/policystore) — An Amazon Verified Permissions policy store — the container for Cedar policies, policy templates, and a schema. Authorization requests (`IsAuthorized`) are evaluated against all policies in a store.
- [PolicyStoreAlias](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/verifiedpermissions/policystorealias) — A named alias for a Verified Permissions policy store. Aliases let callers reference a policy store by a stable name (e.g. in `IsAuthorized` requests) so the underlying store can be swapped without reconfiguring clients.
- [PolicyTemplate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/verifiedpermissions/policytemplate) — A Cedar policy template in a Verified Permissions policy store. Templates contain `?principal` / `?resource` placeholders; template-linked policies instantiate the template for a concrete principal and resource, and every linked policy automatically picks up template updates.
- [PollForJobs](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/codepipeline/pollforjobs) — Runtime binding for `codepipeline:PollForJobs` — fetches pending jobs for a custom action type so a job worker can claim and execute them. Valid only for action types with `Custom` in the owner field; returned jobs include the temporary artifact-store credentials (as `Redacted` values) and any secret configuration values.
- [Portfolio](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/servicecatalog/portfolio) — An AWS Service Catalog portfolio — a container that organizes products and grants access to them for a set of principals.
- [PortfolioProductAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/servicecatalog/portfolioproductassociation) — Associates a Service Catalog product with a portfolio, making the product launchable by the portfolio's principals.
- [PostLineageEvent](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/datazone/postlineageevent) — Runtime binding for `datazone:PostLineageEvent`.
- [PostTimeSeriesDataPoints](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/datazone/posttimeseriesdatapoints) — Runtime binding for `datazone:PostTimeSeriesDataPoints`.
- [PostWhatsAppMessageMedia](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/socialmessaging/postwhatsappmessagemedia) — Runtime binding for `social-messaging:PostWhatsAppMessageMedia`.
- [PredictQApp](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/qapps/predictqapp) — Runtime binding for `qapps:PredictQApp`.
- [PrefixList](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/prefixlist) — A managed prefix list is a named, reusable set of CIDR blocks that you reference by ID from security group rules and route tables. Instead of duplicating the same IP ranges across many rules, you maintain them in one place and every rule that references the list picks up changes automatically.
- [PreparedStatement](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/athena/preparedstatement) — An Amazon Athena prepared statement — a named, parameterized SQL statement saved in a workgroup and run with `EXECUTE name USING ...`. Identity is the `(workGroup, statementName)` pair; the `queryStatement` and `description` are updatable in place.
- [PrepareQuery](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/timestream/preparequery) — Runtime binding for `timestream-query:PrepareQuery` — validate a SQL query against a Timestream Table and inspect its result schema and parameter mappings without running it.
- [Preset](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mediaconvert/preset) — An AWS Elemental MediaConvert output preset — a reusable, named bundle of output settings (container, video codec/resolution/bitrate, audio, and captions) that job templates and jobs reference to produce one output.
- [PresignGetObject](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/s3/presigngetobject) — Mint presigned download (GET) URLs for objects in a Bucket.

- [PrincipalPortfolioAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/servicecatalog/principalportfolioassociation) — Grants an IAM principal (user, group, or role) access to a Service Catalog portfolio, allowing it to browse and launch the portfolio's products.
- [PrivateDnsNamespace](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudmap/privatednsnamespace) — An AWS Cloud Map private DNS namespace — the DNS-based service registry that ECS Service Connect and `serviceRegistries` point at. Services registered in the namespace are discoverable inside the associated VPC via DNS (`{service}.{namespace}`) and from anywhere via the `DiscoverInstances` API.
- [Probe](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mediaconvert/probe) — Runtime binding for `mediaconvert:Probe` — analyze an input media file in S3 (or over HTTPS) and get back its container, codecs, frame rate, resolution, track layout, and captions, to drive transcoding decisions at runtime.
- [Product](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/servicecatalog/product) — An AWS Service Catalog product — a CloudFormation-backed offering (or Terraform/external equivalent) with one or more provisioning artifacts (versions) that principals can launch from a portfolio.
- [Profile](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/b2bi/profile) — An AWS B2B Data Interchange (B2BI) customer profile. A profile is the mechanism used to model a distinct private network; you can have up to five profiles per account. Profiles are credential-free and fully self-service, so their lifecycle is directly testable.
- [Profile](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/rolesanywhere/profile) — An IAM Roles Anywhere profile — the list of IAM roles that the Roles Anywhere service is trusted to assume for authenticated certificate identities, optionally intersected with managed policies and an inline session policy.
- [Profile](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/route53profiles/profile) — An Amazon Route 53 Profile — a reusable container of DNS configuration (private hosted zones, Resolver rules, and DNS Firewall rule groups) that can be associated with many VPCs at once.
- [ProfileAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/route53profiles/profileassociation) — An association between a Route 53 Profile and a VPC. Once the association completes, every DNS resource attached to the Profile (private hosted zones, Resolver rules, DNS Firewall rule groups) takes effect in the VPC.
- [ProfilePermission](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/signer/profilepermission) — A cross-account permission on an AWS Signer signing profile — one statement in the profile's resource policy granting another AWS account (or IAM identity) a Signer action such as `signer:StartSigningJob`. The Signer counterpart of CloudFormation's `AWS::Signer::ProfilePermission`.
- [ProfileResourceAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/route53profiles/profileresourceassociation) — An attachment of a DNS resource to a Route 53 Profile. Attach private hosted zones, Resolver rules, or DNS Firewall rule groups; every VPC the Profile is associated with picks up the resource.

- [Project](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/databrew/project) — An AWS Glue DataBrew project — the interactive workspace binding a dataset to a recipe's working version. The project definition is free; costs only accrue when an interactive session is started in the console.

- [QueueSink](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sqs/queuesink) — A batching sink over SQS `SendMessageBatch` (10 entries / 256 KiB per call). Per-entry failures with `SenderFault: false` (throttling, internal errors) are retried on a bounded schedule; `SenderFault: true` failures are permanent and dropped. Exhausting retries fails the sink with a typed `BatchRetryExhaustedError` carrying the stranded entries.

- [RecognizeUtterance](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lexv2/recognizeutterance) — Runtime binding for `lex:RecognizeUtterance` — send user text or audio to an Amazon Lex V2 bot alias. Unlike `RecognizeText`, the response's `messages`/`sessionState`/`interpretations` come back gzip-compressed and base64-encoded, and an `audioStream` reply is available for voice bots.

- [ReEncryptData](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/reencryptdata) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:ReEncryptData` — decrypts ciphertext under the incoming Key and re-encrypts it under the outgoing Key entirely inside the service; the plaintext never leaves AWS Payment Cryptography. At least one side must be a DUKPT Base Derivation Key or a dynamic (TR-31 wrapped) key — the service rejects plain symmetric-to-symmetric re-encryption with `ValidationException: KeyUsages not allowed for this operation`. Provide `ReEncryptDataHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.

- [RoomMessageReviewEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ivschat/roommessagerevieweventsource) — Event source connecting an IVS Chat Room's message review handler to the hosting Lambda function — every message sent to the room is synchronously reviewed (allow / modify / deny) by the handler before delivery.
- [RoomMessageReviewEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lambda/roommessagerevieweventsource) — Connects an IVS Chat room's message review handler to the current Lambda function.

- [Rotation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ssmcontacts/rotation) — An Incident Manager on-call rotation — a recurring schedule that rotates engagement duty between contacts. Attach rotations to an `ONCALL_SCHEDULE` contact via its engagement plan's `RotationIds`.
- [RotationEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/secretsmanager/rotationeventsource) — Event source connecting a Secrets Manager Secret's rotation to the hosting Lambda function.
- [RotationSchedule](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/secretsmanager/rotationschedule) — Configures automatic rotation on a Secrets Manager secret (`RotateSecret` with a rotation Lambda + rules; `CancelRotateSecret` on delete).
- [Route](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/route) — A single route entry inside a RouteTable. A route maps a destination to exactly one target, telling the VPC where to send packets whose address falls within the destination range.
- [RouteCalculator](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/location/routecalculator) — An Amazon Location Service route calculator. A route calculator computes routes and route matrices against a chosen data provider. The data source is immutable; the description can be updated in place.
- [Router](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/website/router) — Shared CloudFront front door with KV-based dynamic routing.
- [RouteResource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apigatewayv2/routeresource) — An API Gateway v2 Route — matches incoming requests (or WebSocket messages) and forwards them to an Integration.
- [RouteTable](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/routetable) — A VPC route table holds a set of routes that determine where network traffic from associated subnets (or gateways) is directed. Create one route table per routing domain — typically a \"public\" table whose default route points at an InternetGateway, and one or more \"private\" tables whose default route points at a NAT gateway.
- [RouteTableAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/routetableassociation) — Associates a RouteTable with a subnet (or a gateway), making that route table govern traffic for the associated resource. A subnet can be associated with exactly one route table at a time; multiple subnets may share the same route table.
- [Rule](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eventbridge/rule) — An Amazon EventBridge rule that matches events and routes them to targets.
- [Rule](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/rbin/rule) — A Recycle Bin retention rule. Recycle Bin retains deleted EBS snapshots, EBS-backed AMIs, and EBS volumes for a configurable period so they can be recovered after accidental deletion.
- [Rule](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/vpclattice/rule) — An Amazon VPC Lattice listener rule — matches HTTP requests by method, path, or headers and forwards them to target groups (or answers with a fixed response), evaluated in priority order before the listener's default action.
- [RuleGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/networkfirewall/rulegroup) — An AWS Network Firewall rule group — a reusable collection of stateless or stateful network traffic inspection rules referenced by firewall policies.
- [RuleGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/wafv2/rulegroup) — An AWS WAFv2 rule group — a reusable, capacity-bounded collection of rules referenced from web ACLs via `RuleGroupReferenceStatement`.
- [RuleGroupsNamespace](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/amp/rulegroupsnamespace) — A rule groups namespace inside an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace — a container of Prometheus recording and alerting rules, supplied as a YAML definition.
- [Ruleset](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/databrew/ruleset) — An AWS Glue DataBrew ruleset — a set of data-quality rules bound to a dataset. Attach it to a profile job via `validationConfigurations` to produce pass/fail validation results alongside the data profile.

Entries the API echoes back in `UnprocessedItems` (throttling, internal errors) are re-submitted on a bounded schedule; exhausting retries fails the sink with a typed `BatchRetryExhaustedError` carrying the stranded entries.
- [TableStreams](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/keyspaces/tablestreams) — Runtime binding for the Amazon Keyspaces CDC streams data-plane API (`cassandra:ListStreams` / `GetStream` / `GetShardIterator` / `GetRecords`).
- [TagResource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sns/tagresource) — Runtime binding for `sns:TagResource`.
- [TagResource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/transcribe/tagresource) — Runtime binding for `transcribe:TagResource` — add tags to a Transcribe resource (jobs, vocabularies, filters, categories, or models) by ARN.
- [TargetAccountConfiguration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/fis/targetaccountconfiguration) — A target account configuration for a multi-account AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) experiment template — registers an AWS account (and the IAM role FIS assumes there) as a target of the experiment, so a single experiment can inject faults into resources across accounts.
- [TargetGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/elbv2/targetgroup) — An ELBv2 target group. A target group routes requests to one or more registered targets (instances, IPs, Lambda functions, or another ALB) using the configured protocol and port, and runs health checks against them.
- [TargetGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/vpclattice/targetgroup) — An Amazon VPC Lattice target group — the collection of compute targets (IPs, EC2 instances, ALBs, or Lambda functions) that a lattice service's listeners and rules forward traffic to.
- [TargetGroupAttachment](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/elbv2/targetgroupattachment) — Registers a single target (instance, IP address, Lambda function, or ALB) with an ELBv2 target group. ECS services register their own tasks, so this resource matters for Lambda-behind-ALB, EC2 instances, and static IPs.
- [Task](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/datasync/task) — A DataSync task — the transfer definition binding a source location to a destination location, together with the filters, schedule, and transfer options that govern each run.
- [Task](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ecs/task) — A bundled ECS task definition.
- [TaskDefinition](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ecs/taskdefinition) — A standalone ECS task definition for bring-your-own-container workloads.
- [TelemetryConfig](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/observabilityadmin/telemetryconfig) — Account-level CloudWatch **telemetry config** (Observability Admin telemetry evaluation) — an account singleton that audits which AWS resources (VPCs, Lambda functions, ...) have telemetry such as flow logs enabled.
- [TelemetryRule](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/observabilityadmin/telemetryrule) — A CloudWatch **telemetry rule** (Observability Admin) — automatically enables telemetry (such as VPC flow logs) for AWS resources in your account that match the rule's criteria.

- [TerminateJob](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/batch/terminatejob) — Terminate a running (or cancel a queued) AWS Batch job from runtime code.

Reference it by name from `TranslateText`, `TranslateDocument`, or batch translation jobs.

- [TopicSink](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sns/topicsink) — A batching sink over SNS `PublishBatch` (10 entries / 256 KiB per call). Per-entry failures with `SenderFault: false` (throttling, internal errors) are retried on a bounded schedule; `SenderFault: true` failures are permanent and dropped. Exhausting retries fails the sink with a typed `BatchRetryExhaustedError` carrying the stranded entries.
- [toQueue](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eventbridge/toqueue) — Routes matching events from an EventBridge bus to an SQS queue.
- [Tracker](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/location/tracker) — An Amazon Location Service tracker. A tracker records device positions and evaluates them against linked geofence collections. The KMS key is immutable; position filtering, EventBridge publishing, and the description can be updated in place.
- [TrackerConsumer](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/location/trackerconsumer) — Links an Amazon Location Tracker to a GeofenceCollection so every device position uploaded to the tracker is automatically evaluated against the collection's geofences, emitting ENTER/EXIT events (delivered to EventBridge — see `consumeTrackerEvents`).

- [TranslateKeyMaterial](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/translatekeymaterial) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:TranslateKeyMaterial` — translates an ECDH-derived TR-31 wrapped key block into a TR-31 key block wrapped under a Key Encryption Key, without importing the short-lived key into the service. The key identifiers live in nested request structures (`IncomingKeyMaterial.DiffieHellmanTr31KeyBlock.PrivateKeyIdentifier`, `OutgoingKeyMaterial.Tr31KeyBlock.WrappingKeyIdentifier`), so the caller supplies the full request; bind every Key the request references so the Function is granted the action on each. Provide `TranslateKeyMaterialHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.
- [TranslatePinData](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/translatepindata) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:TranslatePinData` — translates an encrypted PIN block from one PIN encryption Key (and ISO 9564 format) to another without the PIN ever leaving the service. This is the core acquirer operation for forwarding PIN blocks between networks. Provide `TranslatePinDataHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.

- [UsagePlan](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apigateway/usageplan) — Usage plan for API stages, throttling, and quotas.
- [UsagePlanKey](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apigateway/usageplankey) — Associates an API key with a usage plan.
- [User](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/user) — A user within an Amazon Cognito user pool, created administratively via `AdminCreateUser`. The invitation message is always suppressed (`MessageAction: SUPPRESS`) — declaratively managed users never trigger invite emails/SMS; set a permanent `password` to make the account usable immediately.
- [User](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iam/user) — An IAM user with optional inline policies, managed policies, and tags.
- [User](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/memorydb/user) — A MemoryDB user — an RBAC identity that authenticates to a cluster and is granted permissions through an access string. Users are grouped into ACLs, which are attached to clusters.
- [User](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/transfer/user) — A user of an AWS Transfer Family server (service-managed identity provider). Users are free configuration objects attached to a Server; the server itself is what incurs hourly cost.
- [UserPool](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/userpool) — An Amazon Cognito user pool — a managed user directory that handles sign-up, sign-in, and token issuance (OIDC-compliant JWTs) for your application.
- [UserPoolAdmin](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/userpooladmin) — Runtime binding for administrative Cognito user pool operations.
- [UserPoolAuth](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/userpoolauth) — Runtime binding for the public (client-side) Cognito user pool auth flows.
- [UserPoolClient](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/userpoolclient) — An app client of an Amazon Cognito user pool. Applications authenticate against the pool through a client, which controls the allowed auth flows, token lifetimes, and OAuth settings.
- [UserPoolDomain](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/userpooldomain) — A domain for an Amazon Cognito user pool's managed login and OAuth 2.0 authorization server. Cognito-prefix domains (`<prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com`) provision in seconds; custom domains require an ACM certificate in us-east-1 and can take 15-60 minutes.
- [UserPoolTriggerEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cognito/userpooltriggereventsource) — Event source connecting a Cognito UserPool Lambda trigger to the hosting Lambda function.
- [UserPoolTriggerEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lambda/userpooltriggereventsource) — Connects a Cognito user pool Lambda trigger to the current Lambda function.
- [ValidateAssessmentReportIntegrity](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/auditmanager/validateassessmentreportintegrity) — Runtime binding for `auditmanager:ValidateAssessmentReportIntegrity`.
- [ValidateConfiguration](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/appconfig/validateconfiguration) — Validate a configuration version against a configuration profile's validators from a Lambda (or other AWS runtime). Pairs with CreateHostedConfigurationVersion + StartDeployment: write the new content, validate it, then roll it out. Fails with a typed `BadRequestException` when a validator rejects the content; succeeds with an empty response when validation passes (including when the profile has no validators).
- [ValidatePipeline](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/osis/validatepipeline) — Runtime binding for `osis:ValidatePipeline`.
- [ValidatePolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/accessanalyzer/validatepolicy) — Runtime binding for `access-analyzer:ValidatePolicy`.
- [ValidateStateMachineDefinition](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/stepfunctions/validatestatemachinedefinition) — Runtime binding for `states:ValidateStateMachineDefinition` — AWS's static ASL validator (the Tier-4 check op for the Step Functions DSL).
- [ValidateTemplate](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudformation/validatetemplate) — Runtime binding for the `ValidateTemplate` operation (IAM action `cloudformation:ValidateTemplate` on `*` — validation is not resource-scoped).
- [Variable](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/frauddetector/variable) — An Amazon Fraud Detector variable — a named input to fraud-detection models and rules, typed and sourced from event data or model scores. Variables are cheap metadata objects.
- [VariantStore](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/omics/variantstore) — An Amazon HealthOmics variant store — a container for genomic variant data (VCF) aligned to a reference genome.
- [Vault](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/glacier/vault) — An Amazon S3 Glacier vault — a container for archives in the original (vault-based) S3 Glacier service.
- [VectorBucket](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/s3vectors/vectorbucket) — An Amazon S3 Vectors bucket — durable storage for vector embeddings, queryable by similarity. Create one or more Indexes inside it to store and query vectors.
- [Vectors](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/s3vectors/vectors) — Read-write runtime binding for the S3 Vectors data plane — read and write vectors in a bound Index.
- [VectorsRead](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/s3vectors/vectorsread) — Read-only runtime binding for the S3 Vectors data plane — query, get, and list vectors in a bound Index.
- [VectorsWrite](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/s3vectors/vectorswrite) — Write-only runtime binding for the S3 Vectors data plane — insert and delete vectors in a bound Index.
- [Vehicle](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iotfleetwise/vehicle) — An AWS IoT FleetWise vehicle — the digital twin of a physical vehicle, created from an `ACTIVE` ModelManifest and DecoderManifest pair and backed by an AWS IoT thing.
- [Verify](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kms/verify) — Runtime binding for `kms:Verify`.
- [VerifyAuthRequestCryptogram](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/verifyauthrequestcryptogram) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:VerifyAuthRequestCryptogram` — verifies an Authorization Request Cryptogram (ARQC) during EMV transaction processing under an issuer master Key, optionally producing the Authorization Response Cryptogram (ARPC). A mismatch fails with the typed `VerificationFailedException`. Provide `VerifyAuthRequestCryptogramHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.
- [VerifyCardValidationData](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/verifycardvalidationdata) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:VerifyCardValidationData` — verifies card validation values (CVV/CVV2, dCVV, CSC) under the same Card Verification Key (CVK) Key used to generate them. A mismatch fails with the typed `VerificationFailedException`. Provide `VerifyCardValidationDataHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.
- [VerifyDevicePosition](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/location/verifydeviceposition) — Verifies a reported device position against cellular, Wi-Fi, and IP signals to detect spoofed GPS locations.
- [VerifyMac](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/kms/verifymac) — Runtime binding for `kms:VerifyMac`.
- [VerifyMac](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/verifymac) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:VerifyMac` — verifies a Message Authentication Code against hex-encoded message data under a Key. A mismatched MAC fails with the typed `VerificationFailedException`. Provide `VerifyMacHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.
- [VerifyPinData](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/paymentcryptography/verifypindata) — Runtime binding for `payment-cryptography:VerifyPinData` — verifies an encrypted PIN block against PIN verification data (e.g. a Visa PVV) using a PIN verification Key (PVK) and the PIN encryption Key (PEK) the block is encrypted under. A mismatch fails with the typed `VerificationFailedException`. Provide `VerifyPinDataHttp` on the Function to satisfy this service.
- [VerifySMSSandboxPhoneNumber](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/sns/verifysmssandboxphonenumber) — Runtime binding for `sns:VerifySMSSandboxPhoneNumber`.
- [View](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/resourceexplorer/view) — An AWS Resource Explorer view — a saved search lens with an optional filter and a set of included properties that `Search` queries run through.
- [VirtualCluster](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/emrcontainers/virtualcluster) — An Amazon EMR on EKS virtual cluster — a registration of a Kubernetes namespace on an EKS cluster as an EMR job-submission target. Virtual clusters consume no resources themselves (no cost while idle); jobs submitted to the virtual cluster run as pods in the mapped namespace.
- [VirtualMFADevice](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iam/virtualmfadevice) — An IAM virtual MFA device.
- [Volume](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/volume) — An Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume — durable block storage you attach to an EC2 instance via a VolumeAttachment. Volumes live in a single Availability Zone and persist independently of any instance.
- [VolumeAttachment](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/volumeattachment) — Attaches an EBS Volume to an EC2 Instance at a device name. The volume and instance must be in the same Availability Zone. On delete the volume is detached (and force-detached as a fallback) before the resource is removed.
- [Vpc](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/vpc) — An Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) — an isolated virtual network that is the root of any custom AWS networking topology. Subnets, route tables, gateways, security groups, and instances are all created inside a VPC.
- [VpcAssociationAuthorization](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/route53/vpcassociationauthorization) — Authorization for a VPC (usually in another AWS account) to be associated with a private hosted zone.
- [VpcConnector](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apprunner/vpcconnector) — An AWS App Runner VPC connector. Associating a connector with an App Runner service routes the service's outbound traffic through your VPC (e.g. to reach an RDS database in private subnets).
- [VpcEndpoint](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/vpcendpoint) — A VPC endpoint that connects your VPC privately to an AWS service (or a service behind a Gateway Load Balancer) without traversing the public internet, a NAT gateway, or an internet gateway.
- [VpcEndpoint](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/opensearchserverless/vpcendpoint) — An Amazon OpenSearch Serverless-managed interface VPC endpoint. Creating one lets resources in a VPC reach a collection privately (without traversing the public internet), and lets a network SecurityPolicy restrict a collection's access to only that endpoint. Creation is asynchronous — the provider polls (bounded) until the endpoint reaches `ACTIVE`.
- [VpcLink](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apigateway/vpclink) — VPC link for private integrations (`connectionType: \"VPC_LINK\"` on a method integration).
- [VpcLink](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apigatewayv2/vpclink) — An API Gateway v2 VPC link — lets an HTTP API reach private resources (ALB/NLB listeners, Cloud Map services) inside a VPC.
- [VpcOrigin](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/cloudfront/vpcorigin) — A CloudFront VPC origin.
- [VpcPeeringConnection](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/ec2/vpcpeeringconnection) — A VPC peering connection links two VPCs so resources in each can communicate using private IP addresses, as if they were on the same network. The two VPCs can be in the same account or different accounts, and the same Region or different Regions. Their CIDR blocks must not overlap.
- [WebACL](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/wafv2/webacl) — An AWS WAFv2 Web ACL — a collection of rules that inspect and control web requests for the AWS resources it is associated with.
- [WebACLAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/wafv2/webaclassociation) — Associates a `REGIONAL` AWS WAFv2 WebACL with a regional resource (ALB, API Gateway stage, AppSync API, Cognito user pool, App Runner service, Amplify app, Verified Access instance) to protect it.
- [WebExperience](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/qbusiness/webexperience) — An Amazon Q Business web experience — the hosted chat UI end users open to converse with an application.
- [WebSocketEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/apigatewayv2/websocketeventsource) — Event source connecting a WebSocket Api route to the hosting Lambda function.
- [WebSocketEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lambda/websocketeventsource) — Connects a WebSocket API route to the current Lambda function.
- [WirelessDestinationEventSource](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/lambda/wirelessdestinationeventsource) — Connects an IoT Wireless Destination's uplink traffic to the current Lambda function.
- [WirelessDevice](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iotwireless/wirelessdevice) — An AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN (or Amazon Sidewalk) wireless device — the cloud registration of a physical radio, wired to a Destination for uplink routing and to a DeviceProfile / ServiceProfile pair for its radio parameters.
- [WirelessGateway](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/iotwireless/wirelessgateway) — An AWS IoT Core for LoRaWAN wireless gateway — the cloud registration of a physical LoRaWAN gateway (packet forwarder), keyed by its unique 64-bit `GatewayEui`.
- [Workflow](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/mwaaserverless/workflow) — An Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow **Serverless** workflow — a serverless Airflow DAG defined by a YAML file in S3 and executed by AWS-managed, multi-tenant Airflow infrastructure without provisioning an environment.
- [Workflow](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/omics/workflow) — An Amazon HealthOmics private workflow — a bioinformatics workflow (WDL, Nextflow, or CWL) that is executed as one or more runs.
- [Workgroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/redshiftserverless/workgroup) — An Amazon Redshift Serverless workgroup — the compute half of a serverless data warehouse.
- [WorkGroup](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/athena/workgroup) — An Amazon Athena workgroup — an isolation boundary for queries that pins the S3 result-output location, result encryption, a bytes-scanned cutoff, and whether that configuration is enforced over per-query client settings.
- [Workload](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/eks/workload) — Creates a Kubernetes deployment with an optional service on an EKS cluster.
- [Workspace](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/amp/workspace) — An Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus (AMP) workspace — a logical, fully-managed Prometheus-compatible metrics store. Metrics are ingested via remote-write and queried through the workspace's Prometheus-compatible endpoint.
- [Workspace](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/grafana/workspace) — An Amazon Managed Grafana workspace — a fully-managed Grafana server for visualizing operational metrics, logs, and traces.
- [WriteRecords](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/timestream/writerecords) — Runtime binding for `timestream-write:WriteRecords` — ingest time-series records into a Timestream Table.
- [ZoneVpcAssociation](https://alchemy.run/providers/aws/route53/zonevpcassociation) — An association between an additional VPC and a private hosted zone.

### Axiom

- [Annotation](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/annotation) — An Axiom annotation — a vertical marker overlaid on charts to flag a deploy, incident, feature flag flip, or any other point/range event you want correlated with telemetry.
- [ApiToken](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/apitoken) — An Axiom API token — a scoped bearer token used to authenticate API requests (ingest, query, admin). Capabilities are pinned at creation time; changing any field triggers a **replacement** because Axiom does not expose an update endpoint.
- [Dashboard](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/dashboard) — An Axiom dashboard — a named, layout-driven collection of charts. Each dashboard takes a full document (`charts` + `layout` array of grid cells + `timeWindow` + `refreshTime`) at version `schemaVersion: 2`.
- [Dataset](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/dataset) — An Axiom dataset — the top-level container that stores events, logs, traces, or metrics. Pick a `kind` up-front: it determines schema and how the data is shown in the UI, and **cannot be changed** after creation (changing it triggers a replacement, which deletes the data).
- [Monitor](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/monitor) — An Axiom monitor — a scheduled APL/MPL query that evaluates on a fixed cadence and fires alerts via notifiers when its condition is met.
- [Notifier](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/notifier) — An Axiom notifier — an alert destination (Slack, email, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Discord, Microsoft Teams, generic webhook, or a fully custom webhook with templated body/headers) that monitors target via `notifierIds`. Exactly one channel under `properties` should be set.
- [View](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/view) — An Axiom saved view — a named, shareable APL query. Useful for building starter dashboards, providing canned \"open in Axiom\" links from your app, or pinning common investigations the team revisits.
- [VirtualField](https://alchemy.run/providers/axiom/virtualfield) — An Axiom virtual field — a saved APL expression that appears as a derived column on a dataset at query time. Use these to standardise common computations (status classes, latency buckets, parsed JSON paths) so dashboards and monitors don't have to redefine them.

### Cloudflare

- [AccessRule](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/firewall/accessrule) — A Cloudflare IP Access rule — block, challenge, or whitelist requests by IP, CIDR range, ASN, or country, either on a single zone or across the whole account.
- [Account](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/account/account) — A Cloudflare account (subaccount), for tenant / partner platforms that provision an account per customer.
- [AccountApiToken](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/apitoken/accountapitoken) — A Cloudflare account-owned API token (`POST /accounts/{account_id}/tokens`).
- [AccountDnsSettings](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/dns/accountdnssettings) — The DNS settings of a Cloudflare account (`/accounts/{account_id}/dns_settings`) — the account-wide `enforceDnsOnly` override and the default DNS settings applied to every new zone (`zoneDefaults`).
- [AccountEntrypoint](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/ruleset/accountentrypoint) — A Cloudflare Ruleset phase entrypoint for an account.
- [AccountResourceTags](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/tags/accountresourcetags) — Key/value tags attached to an account-level Cloudflare resource via the unified resource-tagging API (open beta).
- [AccountSetting](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/workers/accountsetting) — The account-wide Workers settings singleton (`/accounts/{account_id}/workers/account-settings`): the default usage model for new Workers and the Green Compute flag for scheduled Workers.
- [Address](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/email/address) — A verified destination email address on the account.
- [AddressMap](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/addressing/addressmap) — A Cloudflare Address Map — assigns account-owned or Cloudflare-assigned static IPs to zones (BYOIP / Enterprise static IPs).
- [AI](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/workers/ai) — The native Cloudflare Workers AI binding — run inference on Workers AI models directly from a Worker, with no AI Gateway (or any other cloud resource) required. This is the plain `{ type: \"ai\" }` Worker binding: the runtime value is the same `env.AI` handle you would declare in `wrangler.json`.
- [AllowPolicy](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/email/allowpolicy) — A Cloudflare Email Security (Area 1) allow policy — exempts messages matching a sender/recipient pattern from detections.
- [App](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/calls/app) — A Cloudflare Realtime (formerly \"Calls\") SFU application.
- [App](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/flagship/app) — A Cloudflare Flagship app — a container for feature flags.
- [App](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/realtimekit/app) — A Cloudflare RealtimeKit app — the organizational container for RealtimeKit meetings, presets, and webhooks.
- [Application](https://alchemy.run/providers/cloudflare/access/application) — A Cloudflare Zero Trust Access application.
